c.tagline: France's gastronomic capital, built on two rivers and Renaissance light.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered and wait at ranks outside major stations; street-hailing is uncommon, so ride-hail apps (Uber, Bolt, FreeNow) are widely used and often cheaper.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; 15 is the SAMU medical line and 17 the police.

solo.f: Safety index is the main factor (55/100)

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around Part-Dieu and Bellecour; caution in parts of La Guillotière at night

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed Renaissance old town below Fourvière hill, a warren of cobbled streets, traboule passageways, bouchon restaurants, and the Saint-Jean cathedral; best for first-timers who want history within walking distance.

The central peninsula between the Rhône and Saône rivers, home to Place Bellecour, the opera, department stores, and the densest cluster of restaurants and cafes; the convenient walkable base for a first visit.
The steep former silk-weavers' hill, now a bohemian village of artist studios, indie boutiques, leafy squares, and a lively daily market; suits travelers after arts, character, and a local feel.
A regenerated former docklands at the tip of the peninsula where the rivers meet, with the striking Musée des Confluences, a waterfront mall, and modern architecture; calmer and good for families.
A buzzing, multicultural quarter across the Rhône packed with cheap eats, student bars, and late-night spots; suits younger travelers who want nightlife and diversity on a budget.
lodging: Cour des Loges Lyon, A Radisson Collection Hotel

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: The Métro runs roughly 5:00am to 12:30am (until ~1:00am on Fri–Sat); Pleine Lune night buses cover the late hours on weekends.
transit.note: Two funiculars (ficelles) climb from Vieux Lyon up to Fourvière and Saint-Just and are part of the standard TCL network.
transit.pay: The network is run by TCL. Buy a single ticket (€2.00, ~US$2.20), a 10-ride carnet, or a day pass at metro machines and tabacs, or use the TCL app; contactless bank cards also work on validators. One ticket covers metro, tram, funicular, and bus with free transfers within an hour.

transit.m: Rhônexpress tram to Part-Dieu (~30 min, every 15 min)
Taxi to city center (30-40 min, flat fare)

tip.r: Service is included by law (service compris); rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière
This ornate 19th-century basilica crowns Fourvière hill and offers Lyon's most breathtaking panoramic views over the Saône and the city's red rooftops.
Vieux Lyon (Old Lyon)
One of Europe's largest Renaissance districts, its maze of cobbled lanes and pastel facades makes it a UNESCO World Heritage showpiece and a photographer's dream.
Place Bellecour
One of the largest open squares in Europe, this elegant plaza anchors the Presqu'île and offers sweeping views to Fourvière hill.
Cathédrale Saint-Jean-Baptiste
A striking Gothic-Romanesque cathedral in Vieux Lyon famed for its 14th-century astronomical clock and riverside setting.
Fourvière Roman Theatre (Ancient Theatre of Fourvière)
These remarkably preserved 1st-century BC Roman ruins still host concerts today, offering a dramatic glimpse into Lyon's Gallo-Roman past.
Parc de la Tête d'Or
France's largest urban park boasts a picturesque lake, botanical gardens, and a free zoo, making it a favorite for peaceful, scenic strolls.
Musée des Confluences
This futuristic, crystal-and-cloud-shaped museum at the meeting point of the Rhône and Saône rivers is as visually striking as the exhibits inside.
Hôtel de Ville de Lyon
This grand 17th-century city hall on Place des Terreaux is one of France's most opulent municipal buildings, fronted by the famous Bartholdi fountain.
Traboules de Lyon
These hidden passageways threading through Renaissance buildings are a uniquely Lyonnais secret, revealing stunning courtyards and spiral staircases.
Fresque des Lyonnais
A massive, photorealistic trompe-l'œil mural depicting 30 famous Lyonnais figures, it's one of the city's most Instagrammed pieces of street art.

train.note: Almost all fast trains use Gare de Lyon-Part-Dieu; a few also call at Perrache, and the airport station Saint-Exupery TGV is a separate stop on the LGV, so read your ticket carefully. TGVs reach Paris in about 2 hours and Marseille in about 1h40m. The Barcelona service is run by Renfe on Fridays to Mondays and must be booked on renfe.com, while the Turin and Milan trains are shared between Trenitalia's Frecciarossa and SNCF and are sold on each operator's own site - fares differ sharply between them. Eurostar's direct London-Lyon train has not run since 2019, so travel via a change at Paris or Lille.

bus.note: International and long-distance coaches leave from the Perrache coach station, built into the Perrache transport interchange, with some services also using Part-Dieu Villette. Geneva is about 2h30m by coach, Turin around 4h30m and Barcelona 8-9 hours overnight. Tickets are online-only for FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus; regional Cars du Rhone and Cars Region services to the Beaujolais and the Alps are paid for on board. Passport or ID card is required for Spanish and Italian departures.

ferry.note: Lyon stands at the confluence of the Rhone and Saone, some 300 km from the sea, so there are no ferries. Navig'Inter runs sightseeing and dinner cruises on the Saone from the Quai des Celestins, and river cruise ships bound for Avignon and Arles tie up on the Rhone quays, but neither is scheduled transport. The nearest ferry port is Marseille, about 1h40m away by TGV.

half.name: Vienne

half.name: Beaujolais wine region
